title.narrative: A network of graduates providing consulting support is being developed. Extensive information campaigns have been conducted on the possibilities of using digital tools for education, entrepreneurship, communications, public services, etc

description.narrative: The Output is to be implemented and provided throughout the whole life of the Project.Regarding the indicators Awareness of the target groups and Level of understanding of the importance of developing key skills for migrants, society as a whole extensive information campaigns have been conducted since the very start of the work on the project activities. These campaigns included:(i) Several introductory and informative meetings were held in May, July and November 2021 with all representatives of TG4.(ii) Some more than 2,500 potential beneficiaries of the project, representatives of TG1,2,3, were familiarized with the tasks and activities of the project within the framework of surveys ;iii) 2 press releases were published on the 02.02.2021 and the 10.08.202 respectfully.(iv) 3 round tables were held, namely: reation and development of elearning resources (on the 24.09.2021), Drawing up pedagogical scenarios for the development of educational ecourses (on the 15.10.2021) and Development of the potential of migrant workers and recognition of qualifications: challenges, tools, solutions (on the 26.10.20210) with a total of 46 participants from target groups TG4,5 with a total of 46 participants from target groups TG4,5;v) 3 workshops were held in Issykkul, Naryn and Osh pilot regions on the 26.07.2021, on the 28.07.2021 and the 30.07.2021 and in a combined onplace and online mode with a total of participants 122 from target groups TG4,5 (including 79 offline and 43 online);(vi) An international conference Promotion of financial, social and digital inclusion and gender equality of young migrants of Kyrgyzstan was held on the 26.11.2021. (102 participants, including 83 offline and 19 online; Bulgaria, Latvia, Russian Federation, Kyrgyzstan);(vii) Within the framework of the project, a website of the Project has been developed, which contains basic information about the activities of the project. https://equality.inaqa.com/ . The website is in the process of further improvement aimed at providing more thorough information for the different target groups.(viii) Separate information sites/channels in the social networks Facebook, Instagram and Youtube were created and constantly administered. All the main events and useful information on the implementation of the project were regularly also reflected on the pages in the social networks of the project, available via the following links: https://www.facebook.com/equality.kg , https://www.instagram.com/equality.kg/ , and https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCnIPGxpu6d9cYMLRyRS4u1g/featured) .(ix) An informational article on the main directions of the projects activities was also published in the newspaper of the Russian Federation, given that more than 80% of labor migrants are in the Russian Federation;x) To visualize the activities of the project, 2 flyers and 2 posters (in Kyrgyz and Russian) were also developed and printed in 500 and 120 copies.

title.narrative: Development and promotion of social and educational policies to support and expand financial and social inclusion, gender equality for vulnerable groups of young migrants, including women in the KR through the development of innovative digital skills.

description.narrative: The Work for ensuring Outcome 2 was launched. In order to ensure the necessary adapted module to respond in full to the needs of the migrants, the labour markets in the countries where they work, as well in order to take into account the opinion of all the project stakeholders, a questionnaire study was organized both on a nationwide scale and in the regions of the Projects, as well as with intention to cover also the representatives of the Kyrgyz migrant communities in the Russian Federation and Kazakhstan. The results from the questionnaire survey were used for defining in greater details the scope and the content of the educational modules and the necessary educational and teaching materials.The Bulgarian Lead Beneficiary (Lead Partner) provided information materials from the European skills and jobs survey (ESJS), from the series of material and surveys called Guidance for immigrants, and from the labour market and guidance materials prepared for CEDEFOP, other materials and studies from other European educational and research institutions (Annex 29). The Laed Beneficiary provided an explicit training for the linkage between the EQF, NQF, ECVET, ECTS, EuroPass and the other European educational transparency tools and they presence and notification un the educational and teaching material (state educational standards, training plans, qualification certificates and etc.).At the moment no significant change in updated logical matrix of the Project beside setting the year 2021 for the initial sets of ready adapted modules and educational and teaching materials and the year 2022 for the final version of all adapted modules and educational and teaching materials, as the respective reference years.

A general good will of collaboration and assisting the achievement of the project outcomes and outputs have been expressed by all the Kyrgyz government agencies and public institutions. A very positive step is the creation of the new Ministry of Labour and Social Security and Migration of the Kyrgyz Republic which supposed to which supposed to exercise the necessary policy for the overall governing and regulating of the migration process. Ministry of Labour and Social Security and Migration of the Kyrgyz Republic, the State agencies for youth affairs, physical culture and sports of the Kyrgyz Republic, the regional administrations of the IssykKul, Naryn and Osh regions, as well as the The Embassy of the Kyrgyz Republic in the Russian Federation and Armenia have also declared their interest in and readiness to cooperate for the project implementation. Numerous business associations employing Kyrgyz migrants (in the Russian Federation and in Kyrgyzstan) have also expressed their intention for active involvement in the project implementation. A major issue here is the lack of a separate government agency which is in charge of the vocational education and training in the Kyrgyz Republic. As for TG5, the sector of the vocational education and training(the VET sector) that will cover also the educational segment of the migrant has been left for several years as a subject of policy making, decision taking and monitoring split between several institutions such as the Ministry of Education and Science and Ministry of Health. The VET sector for adults is in fact in underdeveloped stage existing only as providing training courses for unemployed persons without the necessary awarding of formal qualification. Certificates are being issued without any reference to neither EQF, NQF and to the existing national educational standards. EQF, NQF, and ECVET as a system are virtually unknown among the VET providers. The sector of the formal vocational education in the field of secondary education suffers of lack of correspondence with the educational offers of the Universities and the Higher Educational Institutions in Kyrgyz Republic. Overlapping of the provided qualifications by the VET sector of secondary schools and the sector of the Higher Education Institutions is often common. The existing state educational VET standards do not reflect the EQF, the NQF of the Kyrgyz Republic and ECVET system.In regards to all the above discovered frame of interactions among the stakeholders, in the updated logical framework of the Project it will be suggested to have as a new source and means of verification by the name of Officially submitted policy recommendation to the Kyrgyz national authorities, which also shall contain the suggestions for creation of national VET agency functioning on the triparty principle (like in the most of the EU countries in involving representation of the public authorities, the VET provider and the employers organizations and the trade unions) and introduction of a gradual policy for adapting of the State educational standards in VET in compliance withTG1 and TG2 the EQF, NQF of Kyrgyzstan and the ECVET system.
